utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, we only have limited time this morning but I only took one hour and 17 minutes with this witness in chief yesterday. I'll be very anxious to start the witness K5. In order to do so, I will have to summon him now because he's some distance away. It would be helpful to know if the Court has any preliminary views as to how much cross-examination time will be allowed to the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Since the witness isn't here -- I must say the Trial Chamber are doubtful if he's added very much to our store of information so far all with respect to the previous witness. Perhaps the Prosecution might like to consider how necessary it is to call --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I think he is the last witness of this particular category and a full-out important part of the story but, Your Honour, yes, I take the point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, you can have until the adjournment for cross-examination of this witness. Bear in mind what I've said, that we've heard much of this information before, and we're not going to be assisted by argument about political matters. You've heard what our views about those things are and the relevance of it and the relevance of the evidence. Let's have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have I understood you correctly? You're limiting my cross-examination of this witness too to one and a half hours, in fact; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You've already had seven minutes, so it will be something in the order of one hour, 40 minutes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Milosevic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said in 1990, that you lost your job. However, the bank you worked in went bankrupt that same year, 1990; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You yourself said that it was the process of liquidation. It's the expression you yourself used meaning bankruptcy.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the constitutional changes, the Serbian regime wanted to have its control over the whole Kosova economy. That was with bank full rights in all the community of the banks of the former Yugoslavia. It had the right to have its foreign relations. It had its own swift code. It was an economic institution with full rights. And I was never told of any bankruptcy or something similar. You can verify that looking at its statements and balance sheets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us not waste time on this so as not to waste time as to what authority the bank had. There's no dispute that the bank operated in accordance with the rules and that it was authorised to work, but I'm talking about something else. When a bank ceases to be capable of fulfilling its obligations, it goes into receivership. You yourself said that in your statement. Do you know that the legal consequences, according to the law, of process of receivership is the secession of employment of the staff, and during that process only a minimum number of staff members are kept employed until the process is completed?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's suppose for a moment that you are right. How, then, can you explain that no single Serb was laid off in the course of this process?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't believe that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: This is presumably something that we can find out from documentation as to whether the bank did go into liquidation or not.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that you are quite right, because at least as far as banks are concerned, everything can be found in documents. As for the liquidation of the bank, that is even stated in the witness's statement on page 4, paragraph 3. But let us move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement, on page 2, paragraph 6, you say that the Albanians worked together with the Serbs and all of them got on very well. How is it possible that when, only a couple of lines up, you said that the Serbs and Albanians hated each other?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a minimum professional relationship at work, and this minimum relationship was based on the goodwill of the majority of the Albanians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this atmosphere of good relationship was not based on the goodwill of the Serbs working there?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already gave the answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You spoke about the constitutional amendments of 1989. Were the Albanians satisfied with the constitutional provisions envisaged by the 1974 constitution, those provisions that you objected to being changed in 1989? Were they satisfied with the amendment to the constitution made in 1974?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not fully satisfied, and this could be seen from the peaceful protests that were organised in 1981.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The demand at those demonstrations was a republic for Kosovo, was it not?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true, and the protests of 1981 paved the first steps to democracy in Europe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And according to 1974 constitution, was Kosovo a component part of the territory of the Republic of Serbia and the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not in a position to speak about it as an expert, but I can say that Kosova was part of Serbia and a constituent part of the former Yugoslav Federation, with a right to veto.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Kosovo was a part of Serbia, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. Let us not get into argument. He has given his answer. As far as it's a matter of law, we will be able to determine it, and there's no point arguing with the witness about it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't consider this to be an argument.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you still consider Kosovo to be a part of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You mentioned the 1981 demonstrations. Do you know that after those demonstrations in 1981, until the end of the 1980s, more than 50.000 Serbs and Montenegrins left Kosovo? Yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know that even before those demonstrations, in the period from 1968 up to then, under pressure, more than 30.000 Serbs left Kosovo, up to 1981? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pressure against the Serbs was a political term, and it represented a notorious syndrome against the Albanians, as if allegedly the Serb women were violated and Serb cemeteries were destroyed, and so on. In fact, that was not the truth. There were also demonstrations staged by Belgrade aimed at discrediting the Albanians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that means that the pressure on the Serbs was made up and that these 50.000 up to 1981 and 30.000 after 1981 left Kosovo because of fabricated pressures; is that what you're claiming?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that the figures are not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is the phenomenon correct?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were fabricated phenomena by the regime, by the Serb regime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it correct that in police patrols that were introduced after 1981, that those patrols were composed of Albanians and Serbs, that they were always ethnically mixed patrols?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the protests and demonstrations, against which violence was used by the regime, I mean the peaceful demonstrations for the establishment of democracy, the police patrol were wearing uniforms which were not seen until then. They used to patrol in groups of threes, where in all cases they were two Serbs and one Albanian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the patrols were mixed, consisting of Albanians and Serbs?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave you my answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you had no reason to care particularly for the Serbs and that the Albanians were brought up to be cautious with the Serbs and that that applied to you as well.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that period, the Albanians were hindered in every possible way, and they didn't enjoy their natural rights.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is not what I'm talking about. I am referring to your statement that you had no reason to care in particular for the Serbs and that the Albanians were brought up to be cautious with the Serbs and that that was your case as well. Let me read out what you said in your statement. "I saw no reason to care for them, and the Albanians were brought up to be cautious with the Serbs and that was the case with me. I was always very cautious in all business dealings and contacts with them." Why should a child be brought up to be cautious with another child because that child is a Serb?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not respect them, but we accepted them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I'll leave out some questions because of the limited time I have at my disposal. This again is linked to your statement. You said on page 3, paragraph 2, that after Vllasi's arrest, the Serbs started returning to Kosovo in large numbers. Where were the Serbs returning from to Kosovo? And when you say that they started returning, I assume you mean that prior to that they had left Kosovo. If that is so, tell me the reason why they had left Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a special programme in place for the "return of the Serbs" to Kosova. I do not rule out the possibility that for special demographic reasons the Serbs may have left Kosova, but there was an opinion that was ultra political, a tendentious opinion, of altering the ethnic structure of the Albanians. I can argue this by the fact that the Serbs were treated in a -- the Serbs had maintained an irrational attitude towards Albanians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If they started coming back, they could only have started coming back if before that they had left. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already explained that there was a call for them to return, but it was another problem to keep them there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement, on page 3, paragraph 2, you said that I had proposed certain measures and constitutioned changes whereby the status of the autonomous province would be abolished. Is it true that prior to those constitutional amendments delegates of the Kosovo Assembly, mostly Albanians, on the 23rd of March, 1989, voted in favour of the amendments to the constitution of Serbia? Is that right or not?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The constitutional many amendments were put forward for public debate, and all those citizens who had the possibility to express their views, they did so, but most of the people opposed these amendments, proposed moments. But the outcome of the debate was never taken into consideration. An assembly was held under extraordinary measures. The Assembly Chamber was surrounded by -- in the Assembly Chamber there were state security officers. The building itself was surrounded by forces, by police forces, and during the vote, people who were not supposed to be there, not members of the Assembly, cast their votes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that the Assembly did not vote in favour of the amendments to the constitution? Just with a yes or no, please, so that we can move on.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that the Kosovo Assembly did not pass the constitutional amendments on the date I mentioned? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't come to say what I want but what is the truth, as I swore at the beginning, and the truth is that the constitutional amendments were approved under the circumstances that I said, and it was the same Assembly that proclaimed the constitutional declaration for independence the following year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That, of course, is not true, but we'll not dwell on that. In 1990, your party considered that it should take part in the elections in Serbia, but you did not expect to get more than 15 seats in parliament, the number that you had in the People's Assembly of Serbia up to then; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was thinking of the Assembly as an institution, even though it was of a different composition. And you must repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am now asking you something else, because what you just said is not true, and there are documents to corroborate that. I was saying that in 1990, your party felt that it should take part in the elections in Serbia, but you estimated that you would not win more than 15 seats in the People's Assembly of the Republic of Serbia, the same number that you had until then. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not true, because in the programme of the largest party that was created at that time, there was the option of Kosova as a republic equal to other republics in the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. As you're claiming that that is not correct, I have here data provided in the documents supplied by the opposing party, disclosed by the other party. Rugova, on the platform of the Democratic Alliance of Kosovo, number 03037052, and the English version is K021410, saying that on the 6th of September, 1990, during the registration of your party in the Federal Secretariat for Justice, the president of your party, Mr. Rugova, declared in a statement for Oslobodenje in Sarajevo that: "Participation in the elections in Serbia would not give us anything more than we already have, that is 15 delegates in the Assembly, but still we have to prepare for the elections in Kosovo, maybe in Serbia, and in Yugoslavia well." So let me repeat the question. Had you intended to take part in the elections or not in view of these statements made by your party leader?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the enforced constitutional decision -- changes in 1989, Kosova was swept up with a wave of protests because the constitutional changes also meant the Albanians losing their rights de jure in contrast to the trends in Europe and in Yugoslavia where the democratisation was on the way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please answer my question? My question is whether this is right or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness answer. The question was: Had you decided to take part in the elections?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In its programme, the LDK articulated political demands. The aim of the LDK was to channel the political demands of the people, and the part of this programme was the Kosova Republic. That was an option. But what you are claiming is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I cited was stated a year and a half after the constitutional changes based on a document disclosed by the other party. So a year and a half after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let us put the matter to the witness. You've heard what it said, Mr. Rugova said on the 6th of September. Now, can you help about that, about taking part in the elections or preparing for the elections?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which elections do you mean?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You heard what was read out. Read it out again, please, Mr. Milosevic. The witness doesn't seem to have taken it in.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was never any question of taking part in the elections for the Serbian parliament, and this is not true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You said that emergency measures were introduced. Is it true that they were introduced by the Presidency of Yugoslavia because the order was threatened in Kosovo, the integrity of the country, and was at that time the Presidency headed by a Muslim, Raif Dizdarevic. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The measures that you mentioned were military measures, compulsory measures, and everything was done at the -- on the barrel of a gun even though the situation was as you say. Even though the person you said was indeed president.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But those measures were introduced by that Presidency. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You and the president of your party, when Rugova was allegedly elected president of Kosovo, you threatened, on the international stage, that the strategy of your party would be radicalised if the international community continues to ignore your demands. Is that true or not? Just yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I perhaps refresh your memory by saying that in a document provided by the other party, in the English version, K040197, says that the president of your party, in 1992, on the 25th of August, in Der Standard, in Vienna, declared: "Our main demand is independence for Kosovo, and if they continue to ignore us, we cannot guarantee that the people will not opt for a more radical strategy." Is that true or not?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it true that behind this demand for independence, there was a plan for unification with Albania?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true, but it is true that there existed a political platform with three options, presented by Mr. Rugova in his own evidence. If you wish, I can repeat it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me remind you of a document again disclosed by the other party, K0214092. Rugova stated that the borders of Kosovo, between Kosovo and Albania, is unnatural, it's like a Berlin Wall; that the border has divided the Albanians; and that this was in connection with an award of the Foundation for Human Rights of the US Congress, and that the award can be seen as the green light for the unification of Kosovo and Albania. Do you remember that statement?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dr. Rugova led a peaceful policy recognised internationally, and in every statement of his, changing borders was presented as a matter of European integration. And indeed, even if all the Albanian territories in the Balkans were united, we would have a single state with the fewest national minorities in the world.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know about the norms of the international community and the Helsinki Act on the unchangeability of borders in Europe, frontiers in Europe? Do you consider that that is contrary to the European position that you refer to?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not appealing to this. I'm merely announcing -- saying that the issue of changing borders, as you say, in the time about which we are talking, the policy was of -- the policy of Mr. Rugova and the majority of the people in Kosova was for Kosova as an independent state and a stabilising element in the Balkans, which was a good precondition for further European integration.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it true that the plan for Kosovo to break off should have been realised in such a way that Kosovo would first of all come under international control, as a first step? Yes or no, according to your views.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you repeat this question, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the plan for Kosovos to secede should have been put into effect by considering that Kosovo should first come under international control?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What is the plan you're talking about, Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm talking about the plan for Kosovo to secede from Yugoslavia, or rather, from Serbia, and to become united with Albania.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Which plan, or is it a notion of yours?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. We're here in this cross-examination -- in the cross-examination of Mr. Rugova, we presented several documents from which this plan was evident, and the creation of a Greater Albania, so I'm asking -- Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That is what you claim. These things are merely alleged by you. Now, are you saying that this witness was a party to this alleged plan?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course. As --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Were you party, Mr. Merovci, of a plan for the establishment of a Greater Albania? That is what is being suggested.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The LDK has its own statute and programme, and there was not a word about the unification of the Albanian lands in the Balkans. But I said that there is a political platform that, by agreement, all the territories in the former Yugoslavia inhabited by Albanians -- and this platform has three points. And for your information, I can repeat it for you, if you wish, but Dr. Rugova, in his own evidence, did put them forward.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And do you remember Rugova's statement to Der Spiegel that the confederation with Albania is a question of the future? That is contained in the document that was disclosed by the opposing party.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question of the future can never be prejudged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in respect of this question - and you didn't give me an answer, at least the second part - the point is that this can be realised by the fact that Kosovo should first come under international control. Let me refresh your memory. In Rugova's interview to the Budapest Daily, he said that the secession of Kosovo could be realised if Kosovo was demilitarised and if it came under international protection. That is the English version of K02140118, paragraph 4. It is the interview he gave and it is presented in the documents. Is that right or not?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said before -- and, Your Honour, you spoke of a plan which did not in fact exist. As far as I'm concerned, I have a very good memory. I remember very well everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Very well. Let's move on to another area, because there are documents to bear that out. Now, you mention, on page 5, paragraph 4 of your statement, that the State Security interrogated you for several days, but on the occasion you say they did not take you into custody. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was for the first time in 1995, in the first half of 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that you were put in prison?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. We've clarified that. Now, yesterday you were saying that you were in prison for a period of six months. I don't know what it said in the transcript, how this was evidenced by the transcript. But then you said six weeks, and finally, from your testimony, it turned out that you were there for 16 days, because you were in illegal possession of weapons. Is that right or not?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is speculation. Initially I was sentenced to one month of prison. I was released after 16 days, after I put in some -- paid some -- left some mortgage for that. Then afterwards I was released on probation. And the second-instance court revoked the decision, that ruling of the court, because it found it was groundless.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were in prison for 16 days; right?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That, in fairness to the witness, is what he said. He said, quite clearly, giving his evidence, that various sentences were passed, but he only spent that time in prison.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Well, yesterday it was six months, then all the rest. That's why I'm asking him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That was the sentences - he made clear - not the time that he spent in custody.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You say that your brother paid somebody, and in fact, it was a guarantee, or rather, bail, provided by law in the criminal proceedings, and bail means that you have to guarantee, by money or property, that you will come to court when called. Is that right or not?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The way you formulate it is not correct. It's not that I paid money; I just offered a guarantee, that is, my house, as a guarantee for the bail.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Bail isn't paid; it is given as a guarantee. So it was on the basis of that guarantee that you were released; is that right or not?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but that's not money, as you asked me earlier. I didn't pay any actual money.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm very happy to hear that. Now, you claim that you don't believe that the KLA, in its day, sentenced Rugova to death; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You claim that you do not believe that the KLA, in their day, sentenced Rugova to death at one point in time?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm absolutely sure that that is not the case. It is mere speculation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The fact that you don't believe this, does that mean that you're not sure? You say, "I don't believe." Does that mean that you're not sure?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that I didn't believe it. I said I am sure about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And is it true that in 1998 you and Rugova concluded that it wasn't safe to travel around Kosovo, especially in the more remote areas?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was true in the entire ten-year period. We were very cautious and didn't travel because of the dangers of an incident staged by Serbian military and police forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But is it correct that members of the army and MUP were not positioned in these remote places? And if the soldiers or members of the MUP weren't there, then who could have jeopardised Rugova's and your safety?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbian army and police couldn't be in every house in Kosova, but to travel to these places you had to pass through dozens of checkpoints.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you're claiming this, is it correct that it was precisely the KLA, in the course of 1998 and the beginning of 1999, held under its control the remote areas of Kosovo and parts of Latsati [phoen]? Do you know about that? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The KLA indeed had various regions under its control, and to visit these areas, as I said, you had to pass through dozens of checkpoints manned by the Serbian forces, and it was a state of war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You, therefore, did not go to these remote areas where the KLA were because you had to pass through the checkpoints and not because you were afraid of your security and safety in these remote areas; is that it?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because we were not scared of the KLA, because the KLA was an organised army, commanded, and was a product of your lack of readiness to solve the problems and to allow the Albanians to exercise their natural rights, and the KLA protected the people from the forces of the occupier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how can somebody occupy his own territory?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not a lawyer. I'm a witness from Kosova. And when natural rights are suspended by force, with the aid of the army, the police, and the destruction of institutions -- I must say that natural rights are the right to life, to education, freedom of thought and expression.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you how somebody could occupy their own territory. Can you answer that question or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He's given the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on to the next question then. Fine. Is it true that Rugova and Hill had a joint undertaking over the draft for a Kosovo agreement, a joint undertaking?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After your agreement with Holbrooke there was shuttle diplomacy, and the G15 and G5 groups were formed to introduce confidence-building measures, as they were called. As a result, these did not meet with success because of your failures to -- because of your refusal, and this led to the international conference of Kosova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Merovci. What I asked you was: Is it true that Rugova and Hill had a joint -- had a joint undertaking to draft an agreement for Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What agreement are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The agreement on Kosovo. Let me refresh your memory and remind you. In the document of the other side, it says that Rugova, in talking to Walker, said that: "We're working on Hill's draft. It is up to Hill to compile a new draft. Hill knows our demands. We're now waiting for Hill." Therefore, they had a joint enterprise concerning this draft. Did they work together on it? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must ask you again not to refresh my memory because my memory is entirely clear. My answer must be no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. For the record, this is English version 0085325 and 000826 paragraph 2. Let's move on anyway. Is it true, in view of your previous statement about the KLA, is it true that your party and your president, the party president, Rugova, called the KLA extremists, referred to them as extremists? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says here in this document - and for the record the English version is 0085327 - it says: "Rugova, in talking to Walker, stated, `In Malisevo we have extremists. In Malisevo we have extremists, and we cannot forget that.'" Is that true or not?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in any document or any public statement did Rugova ever call the KLA extremists. There were cases in which he called them patriots.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's not waste time. Let's move on. I quoted the passage to you. Do you know why the Russian Ambassador, Mayorski, in Rambouillet did not place his signature to the Rambouillet agreement?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can ask Mr. Mayorski about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. How many members of the Albanian delegation from Rambouillet travelled to Brussels to have a meeting there with Clark, the NATO commander?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, about seven or eight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who were they? Who -- which people went?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only mention Mrs. Edita Tahiri, who was present at this meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And the other seven or six you can't remember. Did Clark tell them on the occasion that the Albanians should get off the streets because in a few days time they would be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but this fact is mentioned, that he was told -- that he told them to stay off the streets because they would be there in a few days' time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wasn't at this meeting, but it was interpreted to me it wasn't a matter of keeping off the streets but of being careful.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they weren't told to go to Macedonia and Albania, yes or no, to get away from there?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not an idea to go away -- of -- it wasn't a matter of going away in any sense at all. And this was a warning to all the citizens of Kosova. Not only Albanians but everybody.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that's what I'm saying. I'm referring to all the citizens of Kosovo. Was it suggested that they should get away from Kosovo? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As -- as you've just said, you have a very nice opinion of the KLA. Give me a direct answer to this question: How many members of your party and immediate associates of Ibrahim Rugova were killed by the KLA after the war?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As I don't have time, let me just remind you, Hakim Meri [phoen] From Turicevac near Srbica, on the 2nd of November of 1999, was killed. Sejdo Koci, also a member of the LDK, president of the LDK in Srbica, in fact, the DSK, he said to the Koha Ditore, on the 11th of November, 1999, that the headquarters of the DSK in Decani, Malisevo were exposed to attacks, maltreatment, and killings. Shaban Manaj, the President of the DSK for Istog, disappeared on the 1st of August, 2000. Sonji Geci [phoen] from the village of Laus near Srbica shot members -- shot at members of DSK families and close associates of Rugova on the 1st of August, 2000. According to the reports --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness answer. Let the witness answer. Do you know -- Mr. Merovci, do you know about these cases which have been read out to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The people that were mentioned mostly are known to me, but it can't be proved with any evidence how they were killed. Work is being done in this direction as Dr. Rugova said in his evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wasn't getting the interpretation at all. Something wasn't working. Or perhaps there was an interruption with my microphone. Everything seems to be on, though. I can hear you now. I can hear now, but I didn't get the interpretation of that last answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You can read it on the transcript, but what it said is it can't be proved with any evidence how they were killed. Work is being done in this direction.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ah, yes. I can see it. I've read it. I read it in the meantime. Let's not waste time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to the AP report, on the 24th of November, Rugova said in Minoka [phoen] that all efforts should be invested, that the killers of Xhemail Mustafa, his associate, should be brought to justice. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The late Xhemail Mustafa was killed, it's true, but it still hasn't been confirmed who committed this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about his Ismet Raci, an official of the DSK and president of the Klina municipality on the 25th of April - the year is 2000 - who was buried in the village of Sicevo near Klina? Is it known who his killers were?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he was killed, but I don't know who was behind his murder.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you claim - and I haven't got the time to go through all the killings - that not even the killings of your activist representatives of municipal boards, prominent persons from your party, that it was not the KLA who was behind all these killings? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that the KLA came from the people, and the KLA never had bullets for Albanians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know about the people killed, Albanians killed and kidnapped by the KLA in the course of 1997, 1998, and 1999; is that it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The witness is denying that. Now, we've been over there for some time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. I have half an hour more. I'm looking at the clock. So it is within the time allotted me by you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the war began, you were in Kosovo. You will remember the conference, the press conference held in the house of Dr. Rugova at which you were present yourself, and as you will remember, Rugova said in his testimony here that there were Yugoslav, Turkish, Greek journalists and others. There were a lot of people there at the time. And there are minutes about that. And he says: "Here I am at home. I've been at home since I returned with my family from Paris. There was speculations that I had been killed or wounded. I say now from my home, not only to NATO but to all the international factors in the world, especially the United Nations, that they should cease the bombing of Yugoslavia immediately as well as that of Kosovo and Metohija. Negotiations and a peaceful solution to Kosovo is the only road forward. We are now thinking differently. This is not a good way to solve not only this problem but any other problem, and we've sobered up." Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, as if it were yesterday. And I can state here that this was a conference, a news conference held in the presence of maximum seven armed policemen and soldiers in which Mr. Rugova, in not a single sentence or word, ever called for the stopping of NATO bombing. I have stated this even at earlier occasions, and I can state it today too. If there may be evidence to prove the opposite of what I said, I can still declare that I will always declare the truth and only the truth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. All right. That's very interesting, because you know that proof of this exists. There was a big press conference. But let's move on. You speak about the arrival of Rugova, of his coming to me, and his life was threatened at the time by Albanian terrorists. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two things are not correct. First that the Albanians have never been terrorists in their history. They have never committed any murders in Belgrade or Skopje, but they have fought for their rights, their natural rights. And second, Mr. Rugova has never been threatened or endangered in any way by the Albanians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If he was not in any danger, why did he come to ask me to save him and his family and to send them somewhere away from Pristina and -- if it was not because of the terrorists?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Rugova and myself came to Belgrade without being a party to the decision that ordered us to come there, and there we didn't beg you or ask you to release us and save us from the danger, as you say, but just asked that if we are free, as you have alleged, you should let us leave Kosova because we felt endangered by the Serb police and military forces, paramilitary forces. How can you explain the murder of Agani in this case?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I was just going to ask you that, because he was one of the victims of terrorism in Kosovo. Have you finally established which of those groups killed Agani?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Part of what you are saying is true. He was killed by the Serb terrorists. And the reasons for his murder were because the distinguished late professor was the embodiment of this peaceful spirit, and he was participant in every process under way in Kosova in the last ten years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I personally regret very much the killing of Mr. Agani. I had occasion to meet him a couple of times. But are you claiming that he was not killed by Albanian terrorists?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You -- you are saying that you regret the fact that he was killed. I don't know that, but the fact is that he was not killed by the Albanians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why are you saying that Serb policemen, when they allegedly entered by force into Rugova's house, insisted to talk to him? If he was under arrest, they could have spoken to him without asking you for that opportunity for a whole hour, simply to restrain him and talk to him. How could it have happened in that way if, as you claim, he was under arrest?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yesterday too that it was the 31st of March. It was midday. A police patrol came. They broke down two of Rugova's doors. One of them was a reinforced door. I went down and said to them that there are people here. And as I said yesterday, I raised both my hands up in the air, and they maltreated me for an hour because I told them that Mr. Rugova is here. But the police told me, "We came here to do our duty, and Rugova is the first man to ask for NATO intervention." Then I consulted someone, and they ordered me to bring down all the members of the family, and this is what we did. We all went down on the ground floor. We got together in a single room, all of us, where we were detained for four hours, without letting us do anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And before that, you were beaten for an hour, according to what you said yesterday. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I was maltreated. And I am ashamed, in fact, of what happened in Kosova, considering what happened all over Kosova, to complain here and to say that I was maltreated for an hour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you said, quite explicitly, that you were beaten for an hour, and the next day you came to a meeting with me. You confirmed now that it was on the 31st of March. On the 1st of April, you had a meeting Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. with me. There were no traces on you. You didn't look like a person who had been beaten. How come that on that occasion you didn't take advantage of the meeting at my place to tell me that somebody had broken into your house by force, that you had been beaten, mistreated, and so on? On the contrary. You said that you were being protected by the police, that you were safe, and so on. Why didn't you complain then as to what had happened to you only a day prior to that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness answer.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In answer to your question why didn't I complain at the meeting with you when, in fact, as you allege, the police were protecting us, I don't know how you understand the meaning of the word "maltreatment." They spared my face, in fact, but in my body they beat me up with their rifle butts. And I don't understand even now why they didn't even kill me at all. For your information, I'm not a man that complains easily. As I said, given the fact that what happened in Kosova, the atrocities perpetrated there, my complaint would be a trifle one. During my house detention, house arrest, we were engaged in a life-and-death struggle, and we could escape or could remain alive thanks to what I'm going to say: One, thanks to God; second, thanks to Rugova's calm and wisdom --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... time.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- thanks to international pressure; and lastly, thanks to my personal instincts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Fine. I think it is clear something terrible happened to you a day earlier. Then you and Rugova came to see me the next day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's a comment. He's answered it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So you claim that I said personally at the meeting on the 1st April that the operation against the KLA would soon be over and that after that there would be no need for large numbers of soldiers and policemen in Kosovo; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement, you claim that I said to Rugova that we had to come to an agreement so that people could come back to Kosovo; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No? And Rugova said to you, when you, as his secretary, entered, together with my secretary, after our conversation - at least, that is what you said yesterday - that it should be said that we were in favour of a peaceful solution and political means. What else was said in that statement except our common aspiration towards a peaceful solution by political means?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a press release, and the word "peace" and "peaceful means" is a very abstract notion if it's not actually realised in practice, and the question of implementation rested with you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is common knowledge what "peaceful means" are. Rugova himself gave you instructions to the effect of what was contained in the release, and that release was published, and you, as his secretary, and Milinovic as mine, drafted it in that way. You confirmed that yesterday, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not true. I did not participate, for any moment, in the drafting of that statement. I was called there by Mr. Rugova because he wanted to consult me and to gain some time, and I said to him that this is just a press statement and nothing more than that, and I told you that usually press releases are not signed. It was a formality, in fact. We just crossed out the word "Metohija" from the text, something which you agreed with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you claim that Rugova agreed to sign the release because there was nothing harmful in it. That is what you said. And yesterday you explained that he told you, for a peaceful settlement, et cetera, that that is how the release should be drafted; isn't that so? Yes or no. Please say yes or no. We have very little time left, another 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When Mr. Rugova called me there, he had the written statement on his hand, and this refutes what you are saying, that I was a party to its drafting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you about the contents. We're not trying to establish all the other details, even though what you said is not true. I'm just asking you about the contents. Yes or no, please, and we can move on.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This distinguished Chamber has the text of that statement. I don't deem it necessary to give an answer to this question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. As it coincides what you said yesterday, that Rugova told you, you're claiming that Sainovic told you a number of times that you were free?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me sometimes just for appearance's sake.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't understand that. If he said that you were free, and repeated those words each time, how then could you have been hostages, when he told you that you could go?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: But the reality proved the opposite. At every moment of our talk with him, we asked him to release us. If we were free, then why were we not allowed, during the first, second, third, fourth, fifth, fifteenth day, to leave?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He told you that you were free to go. Who prevented you from going? Did anyone prevent you from going, from leaving?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serb police and army prevented us, were under your command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you wanted to leave and you tried to leave, but you were stopped by the police and the army; is that what you're claiming now?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At every moment, whenever we had an opportunity to communicate with someone, our only demand was to let us go, to let us -- to allow us to leave Kosova, because we felt in danger there and we couldn't live a normal life. I said earlier -- I recounted here the factors that accounted for our survival.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Merovci, I understand. I just wanted to establish these things. Are you aware of Rugova's statement in Rome, in May, when you got there, that he wanted the presence of international forces to ensure the autonomy of Kosovo but not its independence? Are you aware of that? Just tell me yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember it very well, and he has never said what you are claiming now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, do you know that on the 9th of May -- the press is a public document, so we can easily check. Do you know that on the 9th of May, after talks with the Green Party in Brussels, Rugova emphasised again that the autonomy of Kosovo should be created within the framework of Yugoslavia? There's a Reuters report to that effect as well. Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Is it correct that the leadership of your party in Rome, on the 6th of May - that too has been published - said that it was possible to negotiate autonomy with Milosevic, and Melini [phoen] were apparently surprised when they heard that he said that? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Present at every meeting -- I've been present at every meeting, and I've never heard Rugova say this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. That is what the press carried. You're one of his closest associates. On the 6th of May, as registered again in the news, he stated, in Rome, that he left Kosovo to meet up with his associates and discuss the future of Kosovo, and that during his stay in Kosovo, he had many contacts with the authorities in Belgrade and discussed the possibilities of a political settlement and a climate of trust being established. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that already on the 7th of May, following this statement, a spokesman for the KLA, Krasniqi, said that the leader of the Kosovar Albanians, Rugova, does not have the mandate to negotiate Kosovo problems? Is that true? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not like this. It was different. He said it was not true that an agreement had been reached with his agreement with Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Is it true that on the 19th of May, 1999, in Bonn, Rugova demanded that the international community should not sell weapons to the KLA and that they needed to be disarmed? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You have an Agence France press report about that on the 19th of May. Is it true that your party, on the 17th of May, 1999, said that it did not recognise the government in exile of Kosovar Albanians in Tirana led by the separatist KLA Hasim Thaci? That is an announcement of your party, or rather, a statement made by Rugova in Bonn. Is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question of the provisional government was a matter of the delegation at Rambouillet, and Mr. Thaci was elected prime minister and he was described as Gerry Adams of Albanians, and he has contributed to the resolution of the Kosova question and he has contributed to the transformation of the KLA into TMK, the Kosova Protection Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was not my question. I asked you whether your party had declared that it did not recognise that government. You are saying that is not true, though that is what it says here. Is it true that neither you nor Rugova dared to go to Tirana, as Paskal Milo, the head of the diplomacy, declared that Rugova did not come to Tirana because his security could not be guaranteed in Albania? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, tell me: Wasn't one of the conclusions of the talks between Rugova and Milutinovic precisely the formation of a joint government, a mixed government?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you are under arrest and when you are a hostage, you can say anything. We were only listeners. We were not party to that talk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Rugova mentioned you as a candidate for the presidency of that future mixed government. Is there any truth in that?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is your speculation, and I never even dreamed of this, let alone making a reality of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And do you remember that during those talks with Milutinovic, when you said that you were under arrest, Rugova gave a present to Milan Milutinovic, a piece of crystal, a piece of mineral ore from Kosovo? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that was even televised. One could see clearly the gifts. Very well. You don't remember. You said that Rugova insisted on remaining in Kosovo throughout, and he says that he wanted to go abroad. Now, who is telling the truth: you or he?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both of us are telling the truth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if you say Rugova insisted on staying in Kosovo throughout, and he says that he wanted to go abroad, he asked to go abroad, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That was at one stage, at the end. That was his evidence. So clearly there's some confusion in the question. Help us with this: Did there come a time when Mr. Rugova asked to go abroad?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's no dispute that he did.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Rugova decided to stay in Kosova, because after we returned from Paris, we returned to Kosova, and the bombing started. And the Serbian forces, after the bombing started, their move was for all the Albanians to leave Kosova, and we were kept hostages, and we asked to leave Kosova to save ourselves. We're talking about a time when 700.000 or 800.000 people had left Kosova, and the ethnic cleansing imagined by the accused was already happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Merovci. As I see, I only have three minutes left. Mr. Merovci, from that television in Pristina, the journalist's name Fatmir Sahori, you stated to him, in those days, and that means a couple of days after the Rugova/Milosevic meeting, the following, and I am quoting you: "Rugova has food, a telephone, and all this has been made available to him. After the bombing," I'm still quoting, "I visited, upon my request with Ljubisa Vasic, Pristina and the surroundings, the places where bombs fell, and I saw those craters in the centre of town and destroyed houses and the post office. My offices are destroyed. I couldn't recognise my town. The bombing has indeed contributed to the fleeing, because nobody wanted to leave their town. The bombing hastened up the fleeing of the population, and time will show, I claim emphatically, that the bombing of Kosovo is the main cause for the fleeing of the population." This is a statement you made for television. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was a politically created television, a fictitious one of the purpose of the statement was different. They took that opportunity and asked me several questions. And because of the time, I will hurry in my answer. I will apologise to the interpreters. I have never said for a single moment that NATO has bombed. If -- I have said regarding the bombing that how can you explain the fleeing of Albanians to Montenegro when bombing is going on there too and that not a single Serb has left Vojvodina when they too are people like us? This is all I've said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Merovci, are you claiming that you didn't say this? Because we have a videotape. And I don't want to show it so as not to use up my time. You said, "I emphatically claim that the bombing of Kosovo is the main cause for the fleeing of the population." As far as Montenegro is concerned, it was hardly bombed at all. Do you remember the slogans when they wrote "Bomb us as well because we we're not lepers," and do you know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Have you got the tape here?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will deliver it to you. I will supply you with it. Of course I will produce it in public too, which contains all these quotations of Mr. Merovci's from television. He said, "I categorically claim that the bombing of Kosovo is the main reason for the fleeing of the population."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is clearly a statement in a form that ought to be shown to the witness before he leaves the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Where is it, Mr. Milosevic, this tape?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's in Belgrade. I don't have here the conditions required to be able to communicate properly. What I get I get at great speed. And I only have one telephone line to use, only one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We understand all that. When did you get the tape here?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When someone brings it. In a day perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Can you get it here by Monday?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I suppose I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The witness was going to go back this weekend, having been here a long time already. I don't know whether he's in a position to stay until Monday. It really is very unsatisfactory. This is a witness who was originally listed as our very first witness. He was listed as a witness about to give testimony for several days or weeks, and this is matter that should have been put to him earlier on in the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Mr. Merovci, you've heard what's happened. Obviously you should have a chance of dealing with this particular tape and we should see it, and it should have been put to you originally and it hasn't been. What I shall suggest is this: that we obtain the tape and then we find a convenient time for you to come back to deal with it. Mr. Nice, perhaps you could make the arrangements.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes. I'll discuss them with Mr. Merovci outside afterwards, although, of course, I'll have to suspend any discussion with him about the substance of the matter. I don't know if the Court is asking us to help with movement of the tape from Belgrade to here. The accused, of course, does now have the assistance of lawyers working for him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And typically I wouldn't expect to have to do that and indeed wouldn't expect the accused to want me to be involved in handling his exhibits, but of course if there is somebody coming back from Belgrade and if that person can act as a courier, I expect we'll be able to help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, we shall direct that this tape be produced as soon as possible. And perhaps you could have a word during the adjournment with the witness to see when it's convenient for him to come back.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Certainly, yes. I'd be grateful for the opportunity of re-examining on two points, including one question about this interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's deal with this. Are there any questions from the amicus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to make a comment if you allow me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you. Perhaps I might need five minutes. Five minutes at the most.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The next witness is going to take some time to prepare for. So if you would -- Mr. Tapuskovic, if you would deal with it now, we can then adjourn in order that the arrangements are made for the next witness. Can you deal with your questions now, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I want to say for my own part that you ought to have had that tape here. The Chamber has made every effort to ensure that you have facilities, including two legal associates. You ought to have had the tape here, and your not having had it here today is causing severe inconvenience to the Chamber. It's clearly a matter of importance.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, the information that this tape was found, I was informed of that only this morning. I knew about the statements made by Mr. Merovci because he gave similar statements when he was with me, visiting me with Rugova, that the police were feeding them, buying nappies, diapers for the babies, that they were taking care of them, and they were very grateful for all this care and assistance and protection, and they said the very same thing, but I did not know that my associates had in fact come up with the tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, bring it here. Yes, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have just one single area to cover, and in the English version of the statement, it is to be found on page 4, paragraph 3. I don't wish to repeat what Mr. Merovci said in that portion. I should just like to ask Mr. Merovci, if possible, to give me yes or no answers to each of my questions. Questioned by Mr. Tapuskovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Merovci, I don't wish to repeat what it says in your statement. You talked about three options for which the Albanians were ready to solve the Kosovo status with; right?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you know that Yugoslavia ceased to exist in practical terms. Slovenia, Croatia, and Bosnia-Herzegovina reached independence in 1992 and became members of the United Nations. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean then that the first option after the previous Yugoslavia ceased to exist, that the first option was no longer acceptable to the Albanians, to your party, and Mr. Rugova?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is why we had the option Kosovo independent. First republic in the context of the former federation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1992, were parliamentary and presidential elections held in your parts by the Albanians, the referendum and all the rest of it?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The referendum was held in 1991. The presidential and parliamentary elections in 1992, 24 May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm interested in, Mr. Merovci is the following: Right after 1992 right up until 1999, was there on anybody's side, the Albanians, your party, Mr. Rugova, or anybody else, any other political party, was there any mention of any kind of autonomy, whether it was the 1974 one, 1996 one, and so on and so on -- forth, not to mention all the laws. Was there any mention at all of any kind of autonomy within Serbia or were there negotiations with anybody along those lines?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Following the constitutional declaration and the approval of the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. constitution, there has never been any talks either among the Albanians or between the Albanians and the Serbs about the status that you are talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you wanted to negotiate independence, secession, and you were seeking procedure. You were looking for procedure by which to arrive at that end; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under the constitution of 1974, Kosova was a state constituent element of the federation. Given the fact that the federation was broken up, military regime was established in Kosova and the people opted for an independent --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... given that answer.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it asks for that in the context of the dismemberment of the federation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understood that, Mr. Merovci, but what I'm interested in is after 1992. After 1992, you didn't want to discuss any other solution but secession and independence; right?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because the question of secession made no sense, because how can you secede from a state that is not existing? This is an expression of the will of the people to have their natural rights realised. Independence was the only way to realise their natural rights. We didn't want to have a state for the sake of a state.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, did you, in 1998 - let's just take 1998 - on several occasions, sign demands made by Serbia in the name of Mr. Agani and Rugova because you were invited to attend certain meetings and negotiations or did you not? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some force invitations. Being chief of Protocol, I accepted those invitations. They were meetings based not on any principle at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any negotiations?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because the time when they came --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Mr. Tanic? Did anybody from your party, Rugova or any other Albanian, did they ever discuss things of this kind with Mr. Tanic?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally never knew Mr. Tanic, and I don't think someone from us met him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as Mr. Rugova's secretary, did Mr. Rugova negotiate with Mr. Tanic?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Rambouillet was signed. After the signing of Rambouillet, was it your sole desire, that is to say the Albanian's sole desire, to achieve independence regardless of what it said in the document from Rambouillet, that this was not an option?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every Albanian, wherever he lives in the world, supports independence of Kosova because that represents the will of the majority of the people. And this is the behest we have from the Jashari family who I think deserve the Nobel Prize for freedom, democracy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything about an organisation called FARK, Forcet e Armatosura e Republikes se Kosoves? The Armed Forces of the Republic of Kosovo, FARK.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This question, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have heard it in the media, but I've never been involved in it and I have no comments to make on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that a military organisation as well?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I've never been involved in it, and I know of no details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Because of the time restriction, I won't pursue this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Just two topics, very short. Re-examined by Mr. Nice:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First, in the meeting with Milutinovic, was anything said, regardless of whether there was any agreement, was anything said about some form of joint government?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During that meeting, I was the one who insisted most, actually, that those four people who were with us may -- I asked them to take -- to make the decision to let us leave Kosova right away. We discussed there also what you are asking me. It was in a very perfunctory discussion, but we were not actually concentrated on that issue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we were hostages and arrested people, as I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was it you who initiated the discussion about joint government or was it Milutinovic or can't you remember?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Neither Mr. Rugova nor me were the initiators of any other topic than our release.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My second question relates to this television programme of which it is said there is in existence a videotape recording. The accused put to you the following quotation as coming from your mouth, this is part of what he put to you: "The bombing has indeed contributed to the fleeing because nobody wanted to leave their town. The bombing hastened up the fleeing of the population and time will show I claim emphatically, that the bombing of Kosovo is the main cause for the fleeing of the population." That's the quotation. Perhaps you'd deal with this question as yes or no. Can you remember saying those words, in Albanian, no doubt, but those words yourself on a television programme? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I can say that I -- I can paraphrase that statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a minute. Let's deal with it in a way I find it helpful. Were there any circumstances of which you can recall whereby you may have been asked questions along the lines of that quotation and that you would have acknowledged the accuracy of the questions? Just yes or no again to that.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that I was surrounded by armed police and soldiers. It was a form of pressure. But nevertheless, I remember every word I said. And I may -- I said paraphrase it with 99.9 per cent accuracy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. So do you accept there is any truth in this suggestion that you said these things or that you acknowledge saying -- that you acknowledge the truth of such propositions in a television interview?

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the -- on television, it was an ad hoc, improvised station. It was called TV A. I didn't have a chance to look at it later, but I know it was broadcast two, three weeks afterwards. It was -- I was told that it was cut, it was revised, and I would kindly ask the distinguished Judges, because I insist on your expert -- looking at it very carefully, because it is - parts of it may be made up. Some words of mine may be taken out of context and rephrased. I've said this. How can I answer to this question with two or three counter-arguments, that is, whether Albanians are leaving Kosova because of NATO and fear of bombing, why Albanians, I said, are going to another territory that is again being bombed but feel secure there. And the second I said why not a single Serb has left Vojvodina, Serbia, where they too are people like us. And I further said -- excuse me, Mr. Nice. I wish to say one last thing. I said that indirectly, this can be understood or interpreted to mean that bombing might have had a role. This is more or less what I said. But at no moment did I say that bombing is the main reason for the movement of the people. And I say this in full responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: ADNAN MEROVCI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because Albanians were looking forward to NATO bombing because they considered it the most humane mission of the century, which helped them realise their natural rights.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
