utterances.text: Your Honour, it -- although my questions were in part directed at the possibility of the tape arriving and the witness being saved having to come back, it looks to me as though if the tape arrives the witness will have to come back, and we must make sure that we don't overlook the duty of the accused to produce the tape and then we'll get it translated or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. And it may be that you can -- you might find a copy of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Look for a copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are Albanians who have recorded that programme and have said to me that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Merovci, subject to that matter, that concludes your evidence. However, we must ask you to come back on that particular narrow point of the tape. You could do so at a time which is convenient to you. Perhaps you could discuss the matter with the Prosecution to find a time which is suitable when we have a copy of the tape so that we may get to the bottom of what was said. We're going to adjourn now. Mr. Milosevic, if you have information like that again, which is important and goes to the heart of any cross-examination, will you kindly signal at an early stage that you have it so that the position could be fully discussed. And you should have material such as that available in order to put it to the witness, and if you don't, you should tell us beforehand so that arrangements can be made.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just clarify this point? I don't know whether you heard me give an explanation that I was informed this morning of the existence of the tape. So therefore, it was not possible --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. What I'm telling you -- yes, we heard the explanation. What I'm telling you is that if this sort of situation arises again, don't leave it to the last minute in cross-examination. Tell us at the beginning or put it to the witness at the beginning so we can get matters resolved. Meanwhile, we're going to adjourn now. Twenty minutes. At the end of today, there are some administrative matters which I wish to raise with the Prosecution, but we'll hear the witness first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In connection with the previous witness, may I just emphasise that the documents which I mentioned - and I dictated the numbers of the documents - that the opposite side disclosed, that this should be tendered into evidence as exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will certainly consider that. Now, let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, if you would just introduce the witness, Ms. Romano, and then I have a warning to give him.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will also propose that any identification that might be asked of the witness to be done at the end of his testimony, in order to do it in an expeditious way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think we can go into closed session at the beginning. It's better that we identify him at the outset, in closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Witness K5, so that you may understand your position in this Court: We've seen the evidence which it's proposed that you should give. Some of it is liable to incriminate you of criminal offences. So that you can follow your position, it's this: that you may object, under the Rules, to making any statement which might tend to incriminate you. The Trial Chamber may, in those circumstances, compel you to answer - it would be a matter for the Chamber - but any evidence given and compelled in this way cannot be used as evidence in a subsequent prosecution against you for any offence other than that of giving false evidence or testimony. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, while your father was alive and working, there was an incident where he sacked another Albanian policeman? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his name and why was he sacked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: His name was Avdi Musa, from Ferizaj, and the reason for his dismissal was a document, a high school diploma, and for this reason he was dismissed from his job.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the problem with the high school diploma?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: It was a forgery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he ever come back to work in the police station again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes. He came back when the Albanian policemen were dismissed from their work in 1989, 1999 [as interpreted]. He came back to the police station in Ferizaj. And after he came back to Ferizaj, he telephoned my father and my family and said, "I'm back in Ferizaj and I'm going to take my revenge on you and on your family." And from that moment on, he started to be maltreating me and my family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in which position did he come back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: He returned as an inspector of SUP in Ferizaj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe what kind of harassment that was done to you or to your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: As I said, at the beginning he came to Ferizaj, and after a time -- and he took the weapons from my father, which he had with a licence, and he ransacked my house in general. And after a week, he came and summoned me, without any kind of reason at all, only because I was my father's son, because he had problems with my father.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you report the harassment to anybody?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone to Ms. Romano.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you report the harassment to anybody?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes. After a lot of harassment from him, I decided to go to the police station in Ferizaj, and went to the commander, named Miomir Mitic, and I reported the case and said that we had a lot of problems with this man. He harassed me almost every week, and my family and my cousins and my extended family. And he said, "Okay. We can help you, but you have to help us too."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you describe Miomir Mitic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes. Miomir Mitic was the police commander in Ferizaj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did he ask you to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: He asked me to work as an informer for him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as an informer, what kind of work did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: As an informer, at first I sent him information about drug dealers, about thieves, and ordinary crimes, just to get this harassment off my back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you report directly to Mitic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive any payment for that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Payment. I was paid in cigarettes and in money.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did the harassment from Musa stop?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: No, this harassment did not stop, because, as far as I understood it, this too was organised by Mitic and the police inspectors, the Serbian police inspectors, to have me harassed, even as a police informer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1994, you escaped to Germany. Is it true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes. In 1994, I fled to Germany because I -- I couldn't put up with this any longer. I didn't like this business. So I decided to flee to Germany as an asylum seeker, and I went for six months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you came back to Kosovo - this was in 1995, I believe - you continued to work for Mitic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened in May 1999, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: In 1996, there was an incident in which I was in a cafe with a friend of Avdi Musa, and we had a fight in the cafe because of the provocations to which I was subjected. And then Avdi Musa and Azem Haliti, inspectors in Ferizaj, beat me for three hours on end only so that I would confess to lies. And they accused me of supposedly beating a person called Hajrush Rrysha from the village of Varosh near Ferizaj, allegedly that I had stolen 500 marks from him. And then I was sent to prison for six months. And the Judge, Danica Marinkovic, then released me as innocent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did you have a trial?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes. I was convicted, but I was -- I went on trial, but in the end I was declared innocent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say you were convicted, Witness, you spent some time in prison and then you went to trial. At the end of the trial, what was the result? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: The result of the trial was that I was acquitted and that I -- I had not stolen anything, because Musa Avdi and Azem Haliti alleged I had stolen 500 marks, and this came out as not true, only I had got involved in a fight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did you meet someone while in prison?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes. I met a Serb called Dejan Stojkovic from the village of Balic near Ferizaj, who had the pseudonym of Crni, which means "black."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give a description of this man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: He was a member of Arkan's Tigers and had been involved in the war in Croatia and Bosnia, in the wars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you left gaol, did you continue to work as a police informant?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes. We continued working but separately, he on one side and I on another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what was Stojkovic doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Stojkovic worked as an informer for Mitic but by himself. And I also worked similarly but also by myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in 1998, did you and Stojkovic open a business together?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes. We opened a cafe and started to work, working in a cafe called Mimosa, and we started a business. With the money we earned, we bought a black Zastava 128 car, and we started working. It was a cafe and a bar. But after a few months, the policeman, Jashar, from Vitia joined us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in 1998, you received a call from Mitic. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes. In 1998, we got some information on the phone that we had to go to the police station at Ferizaj. And Crni and I went to the police station, and he went first and I went five minutes later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the police station located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: The police station in Ferizaj is on the road to Shtime near the army building, near what was called the JNA building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you go see Mitic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes. We went to the police station commander, to Mitic, the Ferizaj police station commander. That is Dejan and myself. We went to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Mitic alone in his office?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes. Mitic was by himself. There was also a store -- a warehouseman called Vlada who had his own job to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you meet anybody else while you were in the police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes, later, about an hour later. But first we had a conversation just with Mitic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what was the conversation with Mitic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: At first they gave Dejan and me a document like a sort of permit, and they gave us a TT pistol, 7.68, and he gave us one each, and then we, in the course of this conversation -- and in the course of this conversation ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can continue. What did you discuss?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: We discussed about how Mitic had assembled a list of various things, various tasks that we had to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain? What kind of list was that and what were the tasks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: The list was about the liquidation of Albanians, about who was financing the KLA, who had brothers in the KLA, and point out people for liquidation, about throwing bombs, throwing Chinese grenades in Albanian business premises, explosions, burning houses, jobs of that kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who compiled the list, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: The list was prepared by Mitic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did he want to use Chinese grenades?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: He wanted to use Chinese grenades because at that time, the KLA used this kind of ammunition. And his idea was to use these things in order to blame the KLA for these incidents rather than the Serbian police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the proposed involvement of Stojkovic and yourself in this plan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, Witness. What did Mitic want you and Stojkovic to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Mitic wanted me to go as -- to go as an informer because I was from Ferizaj and I knew the streets and I knew people. And my job was merely to point out people for liquidation and for bomb throwing and jobs of this kind that were on Mitic's list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you said that you met -- you met other people also when you were in the police station. That was one hour later. Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: One hour later, we went to the office of the SUP chief called Bogoljub Bogi from Sterpce, living in Ferizaj. And he was head of the state security from Belgrade, but he lived in Prishtina somewhere, and his name was Jashanin. This was the other person that I met.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they in uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: No. They were in plain clothes but Mitic was in uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened after? Did Mitic ask you and Stojkovic to accompany him to some place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Then we stayed with Bogic, and we went to Prishtina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The three of you went to Pristina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you doing in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: We went there because this was on Mitic's list. And we went to the commander of the special units for Kosova, SAJ, and we went to the police station. And his name, I'm not sure about it, but I think his name was Dragan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why did he need to go to Pristina? Did he need an approval?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: He wanted to go to the commander to get permission to do these jobs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he also mention collecting any equipment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you arrived in Pristina, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: When we arrived in Prishtina, we went to the commander of the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is it -- where is it located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: This is in -- near the stadium, near the Boro and Ramiz shopping centre. The police station was known for short as "92."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you meet the commander there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: When we went there, Mitic introduced me to this commander, and he said that this is the commander of the police in Kosova and of the special units, and said that he had taken part in the operation in Prekaz involving Adem Jashari, and said that he'd also brought a woman from Ferizaj called Besa and said to us, "Can you find this woman for us? We want to put her on television." It was something to do with fighting in Prekaz.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what this special police was, the SAJ?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: They were a special unit, what they called anti-terrorist unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was he in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was discussed there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: All these jobs were discussed, and there was another question of giving us KLA uniforms to go onto the Shtime-Suhareke road to talk to journalists from Slovenia and Croatia and foreign countries, and to take their video cameras and to loot them, and we had orders also to kill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was proposing this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: This was suggested by Mitic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was it approved?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: No, this was not approved. No. It was said that this had to be left until later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did Mitic explain all the targets to the SAJ commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he read out all the names listed in the list of targets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: First of all, Xhafer Morina, Metar Morina, Agim Ibrahimi, Shaban Hashani were to be liquidated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was the plan approved?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: And also Ilmi Recica, and various other people whose names I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll go into detail with the names after, Witness. Was the plan approved?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did the commander provide any equipment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes. We received a KLA uniform, an M-45 gun, Chinese grenades, KLA emblems, Tritol explosives, and we took these with us and went to Ferizaj. And I later went home, and Dejan Stojkovic took these things to his own apartment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, the list contains several targets, and Stojkovic and yourself then started doing the tasks as listed, and you continued throughout 1998. Some of the targets were completed in 1998 and some were done during the conflict in 1999; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what was your first work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: In 1998, it was my first job to go to Manastirice and to leave a letter, which I wrote in Albanian, and this letter had the emblem of the KLA on it and it said that Serbs could no longer use these buses. And then we wrote this letter and put it in the house of the owner of the buses, because he had private buses. And Dejan, at that moment, threw petrol and burnt the buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what was the second one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: The second job was to go to a certain street, where there was a mini market, a small private store, and I went and stood in front of it, with Dejan Stojkovic, and took those goods of value from the store and then set fire to the store.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why was that store in the list?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: This store was owned by someone from Sllatine, somebody from Sllatine, in Kacanik municipality, called Ruzhdi Rudi, who had been giving money to the KLA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Hamdi Komuna in the list?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes. Mitic said that Hamdi Komuna was rich, and he was on the list because he too had supposedly financed the KLA. And we went to his house, and he had a BMW of the latest model in front of his house, and Dejan threw petrol on this and set fire to it and then we fled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember Agim Ibrahimi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Agim Ibrahimi, as Mitic said, was an organiser of demonstrations, and he was a kind of patriot. He supported the Albanians. And he worked as a guard in one of the Albanian schools. And Dejan was supposed to liquidate him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: After a few days, we went with his black 128 car and kept watch on him. We followed him, because he was on this list for liquidation. And he was in a tea shop on the road to Gjilan, sitting, and we followed him, because we knew where his house was. He lived in the new neighbourhood near the kindergarten. And there was a meadow there, and then we waited for him there. And he was approaching. It was night. But he was in the company of another person and a dog. And Dejan was getting ready to kill both these people, but I said, "We don't know this other person. We can't kill both of them," because we didn't have instructions to kill this other person, but only Agim Ibrahimi. And Dejan became annoyed, and we abandoned this mission.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, during this time there was any other person working with you and Stojkovic, or was it just the two of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: There were just the two of us. There were others, and there were more of them later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Shaban Hashani in the list?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes, Shaban Hashani was on the list, and Mitic said that he was headmaster of the technical school in Ferizaj. He was member of the Kosova Democratic League and had taken part in a lot of meetings. He was at the parliament in Kacanik that proclaimed the constitution of the Republic of Kosova. And so he was on the list for liquidation. So we went to him, and in front of his yard he had a -- and then we waited in front of his yard. He had a WC in front of his yard. And we waited for half an hour. His wife came out and his son came out, but he never came out, and so we went back, and without doing this job.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Ilmi Recica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Mitic said about Ilmi Recica that he had been convicted for political crimes. He was an Albanian patriot. And he had information that Ilmi Recica was a KLA commander for the village of Jezerc, and he had his photograph, and he had had orders to have this person killed too, or a member of his family. And Dejan and I went to this person too, and we waited in front of his house, and we waited for an hour. And some women came out, and I don't know if it was his mother. But no, none of the men ever came out, so we didn't do the job.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, there were a couple of bars in the list. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes, there were bars, and our job was to throw Chinese grenades, such as in the Bolero bar, where the LDK members used to sit, as well as the Casablanca bar. And the plan was to throw Chinese grenades there, only because they were frequented by Albanians --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: -- and to ascribe the killings to the KLA. Would you repeat your question again?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you do the jobs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: We went to the Casablanca cafe and we planted some Tritol explosives there, but it didn't explode because the fuse got wet. It was raining. And Dejan went and took the fuse and took the explosives away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to Afrim Musliu?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Afrim Musliu. Mitic had information that he was a member of the KLA. And his house was on the Nerodima Road in Ferizaj, and I had orders to go to him and see if Afrim was there. And Dejan looted his house inside. And we went to his house and waited at his door with automatic weapon, but we didn't find anybody there. And we were masked. And then we disappeared.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were also travel agencies in the list. Can you explain about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes. There were also travel agencies on the list, because Mitic had information that at a tea shop near the mosque, near the old mosque in Ferizaj, there was a picture of a karate club in Switzerland and there were some signatures on this. And Mitic had information that there was a travel agency with members of the KLA. And I went and I took away this photograph at night and took it to Mitic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you steal anything from the travel agency?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: The order was to set fire to the travel agency, with its computers, and to take objects of value.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you take value from the places?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes, we tried. Yes, and we did. We did take these things. We did what Mitic said. We did this job in a travel agency near the mosque.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe what happened, one example? Do you remember one of the travel agencies that you worked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes. The travel agency belonged to somebody called Vladi, and we stole the money that was there and we destroyed the other contents of this premises.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. K5, in cases in which you were ordered to liquidate somebody, you never succeeded in those missions, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I didn't have orders to kill. I merely had orders to point out people. Dejan had orders to kill.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And all you did was that you went to their places and waited for them to appear, and they didn't appear, so you gave up everything; is that it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... again? Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you remember any case where you were asked to liquidate or there were people in the list that you had to liquidate during 1998 or even 1999? Do you remember if they were at least killed, not by you, by maybe by one of the others, other people that accompanied you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes. Some were killed in 1999. For example, in Nerodima village, lower Nerodima, there was some who was lower on the list by Mitic was killed. He was a patriot. He was a KLA. He was on the side of KLA, and he was liquidated. Not by Mitic himself but by other persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will go into 1999 after. During 1998, after doing the jobs, did you used to report back to Mitic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes, Yes. We did report back to him about the jobs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did he do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Nothing. He gave us cigarettes and drinks. He was happy. Then he had his own team. After, for example, a bus was burned or a house was burned, he sent his police team to conduct investigations and to identify that this was not done by a human hand but it was an accident, you know. This is what he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he conducted investigations for the places that you worked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the result of all the investigations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: The result was that allegedly they were accidents. For example, a short circuit or something may have caused, let's say, a certain arson in a house. I mean, the burning of a certain house and not perpetrated by a person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was any incident blamed by the KLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. In Kacanik, there was fighting there. I was also present there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you didn't understand my question. Was, as a result of the investigation, was the KLA blamed -- was the KLA appointed as the organisation or the person who did the work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any document given to you by Mitic identifying you and Stojkovic as working for the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: It was a kind of letter, authorisation with my name, my last name, the number of my pistol. There was a signature by -- Belgrade signature, and a seal, and the signature of Mitic. It was to provide us with some security. When we left Ferizaj if the local police or someone might intercept us at night, we have to show this authorisation for them to leave us alone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you still have this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: No. Out of fear that someone might find it on me, I burned this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you know a group called Black Hand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: I've heard about that when I was in that coffee bar, a Serb police was there showed, Jashar Jashoviq, showed -- told me about this group. He said to me that they were Serb policemen and that one of them was called Dimitri and that he had come from Serbia. I know the other members by sight. I know one of them had worked in the police station in my village, and he was a member of this organisation. And I saw them in that coffee shop --(redacted).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the Serb police who pointed out Dimitri for you the same one that was in -- that you met while you were in the police station with Mitic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, he was the one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what the Black Hand -- what did they do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes. This Black Hand organisation was set up to kill Albanians. Not to engage in politics but only to do short work of Albanians, to commit atrocities, to strike fear among the Albanians, to force them to leave their places, their homes. This is what they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were they present in Ferizaj in 1998?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K5
utterances.text: Yes, they were present in Ferizaj in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Your Honour, you said that you would like some matters to be raised, and I'm getting into 1999 now. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. That would be a convenient time. We'll go on to 1999 on Monday. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Witness K5, we're going to adjourn now. Would you please be back at 9.00 on Monday to conclude your evidence. Would you remember this during the adjournment, not to speak to anybody about your evidence, and that does include members of the Prosecution team. Now, you'll just have to remain there while we deal with some other matters first. Mr. Nice, I mentioned some administrative matters, and it may be convenient to deal with them now for next week. The first concerns Wednesday, the 29th of May, a date on which you have, I see, listed a witness, General Maisonneuve. The first point to be made about that day is that we shall be starting late. I don't know if you've seen the notice. The accused apparently has a dental appointment. So we're not starting until half past ten. Now, that affects the day because, as I understand it, the General is only available that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It so happens today that I received disquieting news from Canada that he's now not able to come that day because again as presently advised, the confirmation letter or similar sent to the address that has always been appropriate for the general before is now said not to be appropriate and for some reason he has not been notified. We first heard of this this morning. Until the time gap between here and Canada allows us to telephone, we can't take matters further. We are dealing with it as soon as we can this afternoon, having been clearly understood by Mr. Ryneveld, whom I think spoke to the general a week or so ago, that he was coming on that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, that obviously is a matter which will have to be resolved. Meanwhile, we have had the opportunity of looking at his statement, which it was -- your application should be treated under Rule 92 bis. There are matters in it which we feel should be dealt with by way of live evidence. For instance, what he says about Racak and what he says about the VJ chain of command. Those seem to me to be matters which it is appropriate for him to give live, although there may be other matters which he can deal with by way of 92 bis. So I mention that, although it may not now be as urgent as it appeared to be originally.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, yes. We'll have to wait and see on that. And of course any revisions arising to the witness list from his definite non-availability will be communicated to all the parties simply as soon as I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The next matter concerns an expert report --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: -- an expert report which we've had from Mr. Coo. I hope I pronounce his name rightly. I've had a chance of looking at it, and really, three points arise for you to consider. The first, I can see no details of his qualifications or curriculum vitae, so if you would supply those --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: -- to support your application. We'll have to consider, I think, whether it's appropriate that he should make the conclusions which he does in the part that I've seen. I understand there's a second part of that report which may be more controversial because that does appear to contain conclusions. And in that connection, perhaps I can remind you of the decision of this Trial Chamber, as it was then constituted, in Kordic about a Mr. Cigar and his proposed evidence. The third matter for your consideration is this: that he gives evidence or deals in his report with such things as the VJ and the MUP and the chains of command and also the constitutional position. What I don't understand, and perhaps you could deal with it in due course, is why you are also going to call a military expert, a constitution expert, and a MUP expert. Perhaps you could give some thought to those matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Certainly. Of course they have already been given thought, and it will be a useful opportunity next week to explain our thinking on them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. And in connection with that, we would wish to have the amicus's submissions on Mr. Coo as soon as possible. Finally, it would obviously be convenient to deal with as many administrative matters as we can possibly next Friday, at the end of the week, and we should set some time aside for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. And I've been helpfully provided with an advanced copy of the Scheduling Order which will have to be dealt with next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: There's the issue of the witness who would, and the Prosecution proposition, be able to summarise the Racakic. And I have another much more general issue in relation to witnesses I was going to raise in any event next week. That will probably fit conveniently with the discussion that will be generated by the Scheduling Order where it refers to insider witnesses. So a quite general topic I want to raise about that, all of which may take some time, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We ought, therefore, to set aside at least an hour next Friday.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes. The discussion about a summarising witness might conveniently be taken earlier in the week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It can be dealt with quite shortly because the arguments have been rehearsed in writing several times before, but that argument would have to be taken before the relevant witness is called to the stand. May I before, Your Honour closes court, assuming you're about just to do that, invite the accused, through the Court, to give little further consideration to the method by which he produces exhibits? Again this morning he lists some numbers and then, as I saw from the transcript when I returned after the second session had started, requests that they become exhibits. He's done that once or twice before and we're still dealing with the backlog. Of course a number does enable us -- a serial number does enable us to draw an exhibit down. It doesn't enable us to do it immediately. We can't simply produce it like a rabbit from the hat and hand it to the witness. If the accused would be good enough to make those documents available either in copy or in sufficient numbers before he asks a witness about them or even if he gives them to us or possibly to the Registry before he starts cross-examining, we will try to ensure that they are copied so that we don't have this problem of a backlog of decisions building up, which we probably pretty nearly all forgotten about were it not for the good services of my case managers who industriously remind me that there are these outstanding issues. So I'd invite the accused's further cooperation on this if he would be so good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, I will be good enough to supply you with a list of the exhibits that I have requested. And as I have understood that my dental appointment on Wednesday is an obstacle, I shall ask them to make another appointment for me so this should not be an obstacle to hearing General Maisonneuve, because I do have -- I would really like to have the opportunity of cross-examining him. I have this fervent desire. So can my dental appointment be put forward or put back or put at any other time? Because I do not want this to be the reason, even if I don't go and see the dentist at all that week. But I have the fervent desire to cross-examine and hear General Maisonneuve, and I hope you won't deprive me of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We'll adjourn now. Monday morning, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 27th day of May, 2002, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 12.17 p.m.,
